topic: Violations Which May Result in Disciplinary Actions
question: Under Alabama real estate license law, which of the following is a ground for disciplinary action against a licensee?
choice_a: Preparing a comparative market analysis using publicly available sales data
choice_b: Declining to write an offer the licensee believes is unreasonable, after advising the client of that opinion
choice_c: Recommending that a client have a contract reviewed by an attorney before signing
choice_d: Making a material misrepresentation to a party in connection with a real estate transaction
explanation: Alabama's license law authorizes the Real Estate Commission to discipline a licensee for material misrepresentation in a transaction. The other choices describe ordinary, permissible professional conduct.
source_note: Ala. Code § 34-27-36(a) (Alabama Real Estate License Law, Art. 2 — Commission authority to fine/revoke/suspend/reprimand a licensee found in violation). topic: Violations Which May Result in Disciplinary Actions
question: A broker instructs several affiliated salespersons to consistently tell prospective buyers that a property's roof is 'brand new' when the broker knows this is false. The broker never personally repeats the statement. Under Alabama law, is the broker subject to discipline?
choice_a: Yes — pursuing a continued course of misrepresentation through agents or salespersons is itself grounds for discipline
choice_b: No — only the salespersons who actually spoke to the buyers can be disciplined
choice_c: No — discipline only applies to written misrepresentations, not verbal ones
choice_d: Yes, but only if a sale actually closes as a result
explanation: Alabama's disciplinary grounds reach a broker who pursues a continued and flagrant course of misrepresentation, including through the acts of salespersons acting under the broker's direction; a completed sale is not required to trigger discipline.
source_note: Ala. Code § 34-27-36(a) (grounds — misrepresentation through agents). HEDGED: subsection (a) is confirmed real (live-verified via a sibling work product on the same statute); the specific enumerated paragraph within (a) was not independently live-verified this session.

topic: Violations Which May Result in Disciplinary Actions
question: Alabama's disciplinary statute includes a catch-all provision reaching conduct that is not specifically listed elsewhere in the statute. What is this provision generally described as covering?
choice_a: Only conduct that has already been the subject of a criminal conviction
choice_b: Any other conduct that constitutes dishonest dealing, even if not separately enumerated
choice_c: Only conduct involving a licensee's own personal property transactions
choice_d: Nothing — Alabama's list of grounds for discipline is exhaustive and admits no catch-all
explanation: In addition to enumerating specific prohibited acts, Alabama's grounds-for-discipline statute includes a general 'dishonest dealing' catch-all, allowing the Commission to reach misconduct that harms the public even when it does not fit a more specific listed category.
source_note: Ala. Code § 34-27-36(a) (dishonest-dealing catch-all ground). HEDGED: subsection (a) is confirmed real (see file note); the specific enumerated paragraph was not independently live-verified this session.

topic: Violations Which May Result in Disciplinary Actions
question: A homeowner has a valid, unexpired exclusive listing agreement with Broker A. Broker B contacts the homeowner directly and persuades the homeowner to cancel that listing early so the homeowner can list with Broker B instead. Under Alabama law, Broker B's conduct is:
choice_a: Permitted, because any broker may solicit any seller at any time regardless of existing agreements
choice_b: Only a civil matter between the two brokers and outside the Commission's authority
choice_c: Grounds for discipline, because inducing a party to a contract to break it is a listed violation
choice_d: Permitted, as long as Broker B does not charge a lower commission than Broker A
explanation: Inducing any party to a contract, sale, or lease to break that contract for the purpose of substituting a new agreement is expressly listed as a ground for disciplinary action under Alabama license law.
source_note: Ala. Code § 34-27-36(a) (inducing breach of contract). HEDGED: subsection (a) is confirmed real (see file note); the specific enumerated paragraph was not independently live-verified this session.

topic: Violations Which May Result in Disciplinary Actions
question: Broker B contacts a homeowner whose exclusive listing with Broker A expired last week with no renewal, and signs the homeowner to a new listing. Under Alabama law, this conduct is:
choice_a: A violation identical to inducing a breach of an active listing
choice_b: A violation unless Broker B pays Broker A a referral fee
choice_c: A violation only if Broker A objects in writing
choice_d: Not a violation, because no valid contract existed for Broker B to interfere with once the listing had genuinely expired
explanation: The 'inducing breach of contract' violation applies to interference with an existing, valid agreement. Soliciting a seller after a prior listing has genuinely and fully expired is lawful competition, not an inducement to break an active contract.
source_note: Ala. Code § 34-27-36(a) (inducing breach of contract — distinguished from lawful post-expiration solicitation). HEDGED: subsection (a) is confirmed real (see file note); the specific enumerated paragraph was not independently live-verified this session.

topic: Violations Which May Result in Disciplinary Actions
question: A salesperson places a newspaper ad for a listed property showing only the salesperson's personal cell phone number and the words 'Call Jane, agent' — with no mention of the employing broker's name or firm. Under Alabama license law, this advertisement is:
choice_a: A violation, because a salesperson may not advertise real estate independently of the employing broker's name and control
choice_b: Permitted, because the salesperson holds an active real estate license
choice_c: Permitted, as long as the ad is truthful about the property itself
choice_d: A violation only if the salesperson charges a fee for placing the ad
explanation: Alabama treats advertising that does not identify the responsible broker, or that allows a salesperson to advertise independently rather than under the employing broker's name and supervision, as a listed violation subject to discipline.
source_note: Ala. Code § 34-27-36(a); Ala. Admin. Code ch. 790-X-3 (AREC advertising / standards-of-conduct rules). topic: Violations Which May Result in Disciplinary Actions
question: An ad for a listed home states the property has 'no known defects' and 'guaranteed to appreciate 20% within a year,' even though the licensee has no basis for either claim. Under Alabama law, this advertising is:
choice_a: Permitted puffery, since all real estate advertising is understood to be exaggerated
choice_b: A violation, because advertising containing false or misleading representations is a listed ground for discipline
choice_c: A violation only if a buyer actually purchases the property in reliance on the ad
choice_d: Permitted as long as the seller approved the wording of the ad
explanation: False or misleading advertising, including unsupported claims about a property's condition or future value, is grounds for discipline regardless of whether a sale ultimately results or whether the seller approved the language.

topic: Violations Which May Result in Disciplinary Actions
question: Which of the following advertising practices would most likely subject an Alabama licensee to discipline?
choice_a: An ad that includes the licensed broker's firm name alongside the salesperson's name
choice_b: An ad that lists the square footage and asking price of the property
choice_c: A 'blind ad' that offers real estate for sale without disclosing that the person placing the ad is a licensed real estate agent
choice_d: An ad that includes a photograph of the property's exterior
explanation: Advertising that conceals a licensee's status as a real estate agent — a 'blind ad' — is a recognized violation, since consumers are entitled to know they are dealing with a licensed professional rather than a private seller.
source_note: Ala. Code § 34-27-36(a); Ala. Admin. Code ch. 790-X-3 (blind-ad / advertising disclosure rules). HEDGED: section/chapter-level citations, not independently live-verified this session.

topic: Violations Which May Result in Disciplinary Actions
question: A seller signs an exclusive listing agreement with a broker. Under Alabama license law, which of the following would be a violation related to that listing agreement?
choice_a: The broker's insistence that the listing agreement include a definite expiration date
choice_b: The broker's decision to hold weekly open houses to market the property
choice_c: The broker's referral of a qualified lender to the seller's buyer
choice_d: The broker's failure to furnish the seller with a copy of the signed listing agreement
explanation: Failing to furnish a copy of a listing agreement (or any other contract) to the party who signed it is a listed ground for discipline. Including a definite expiration date and actively marketing the property are required or encouraged practices, not violations.
source_note: Ala. Code § 34-27-36(a) (failure to furnish copies of listing agreements). HEDGED: subsection (a) is confirmed real (see file note); the specific enumerated paragraph was not independently live-verified this session.

topic: Violations Which May Result in Disciplinary Actions
question: A listing agreement contains no stated expiration date and instead 'automatically renews indefinitely until either party cancels.' Under Alabama license law, this type of open-ended listing arrangement is generally treated as:
choice_a: A violation, because a listing agreement must contain a definite expiration date
choice_b: Fully acceptable, because brokers may structure listing terms however they and the seller agree
choice_c: A violation only if the seller later complains to the Commission
choice_d: Required practice for all exclusive listings in Alabama
explanation: Alabama license law requires listing agreements to contain a definite expiration date; an indefinite, automatically-renewing listing with no fixed end date is a recognized violation because it can improperly bind a seller indefinitely.
source_note: Ala. Code § 34-27-36(a) (listing agreements — definite expiration date requirement). HEDGED: subsection (a) is confirmed real (see file note); the specific enumerated paragraph was not independently live-verified this session.

topic: Violations Which May Result in Disciplinary Actions
question: A broker continues to actively market a property and collect showings under a listing agreement that expired two months ago, without obtaining any renewal or extension from the seller. Under Alabama law, this conduct is:
choice_a: Permitted, because the broker's prior efforts on the listing justify continuing to market it
choice_b: A violation, because acting on an expired listing agreement without a valid renewal is a listed ground for discipline
choice_c: Permitted as long as the seller has not hired a different broker
choice_d: A matter solely for the seller and broker to resolve privately, with no Commission jurisdiction
explanation: A broker who acts under a listing agreement that has expired, without a valid renewal, is acting without proper authority from the seller — a ground for disciplinary action, and one within the Commission's jurisdiction regardless of any private arrangement.
source_note: Ala. Code § 34-27-36(a) (acting on an expired listing agreement). HEDGED: subsection (a) is confirmed real (see file note); the specific enumerated paragraph was not independently live-verified this session.

topic: Violations Which May Result in Disciplinary Actions
question: A licensee representing a seller knows the property's basement floods heavily every spring but does not mention this to a prospective buyer who asks directly about water issues. Under Alabama license law, this failure is:
choice_a: Not a violation, because sellers alone are responsible for property condition disclosures
choice_b: Not a violation, because the buyer should have hired a home inspector
choice_c: A violation, because failing to disclose a known material defect to a party is grounds for discipline
choice_d: A violation only if the buyer purchases the home and later sues in civil court
explanation: Failure to give proper disclosure of a known material fact — such as a recurring flooding problem directly asked about — is a listed ground for discipline against the licensee, independent of any separate civil liability of the seller or the buyer's own diligence.
source_note: Ala. Code § 34-27-36(a) (failure to give proper disclosure). HEDGED: subsection (a) is confirmed real (see file note); the specific enumerated paragraph was not independently live-verified this session.

topic: Violations Which May Result in Disciplinary Actions
question: A licensee is working with both the buyer and the seller in the same transaction but never tells either party that the other is also being represented by the same licensee. Under Alabama license law, this is:
choice_a: Permitted, because a licensee may represent both sides of a transaction without informing either party
choice_b: A violation only if the licensee charges both parties a commission
choice_c: Permitted as long as the transaction closes successfully
choice_d: A violation, because failing to disclose a dual representation to the parties involved is a proper-disclosure violation
explanation: Acting for more than one party to a transaction without the knowledge and consent of all parties is a listed disclosure-related violation; both parties are entitled to know when the same licensee represents the other side.

topic: Violations Which May Result in Disciplinary Actions
question: Under Alabama license law, a broker's obligation to keep 'appropriate records' of real estate transactions primarily serves what purpose?
choice_a: To allow the Alabama Real Estate Commission to review and verify the broker's handling of transactions and funds when needed
choice_b: To provide the broker's accountant with data for annual tax filings only
choice_c: To satisfy the buyer's own personal record-keeping preferences
choice_d: To document marketing performance for the broker's own business planning
explanation: Alabama license law requires brokers to maintain adequate records of transactions so that the Commission can inspect and verify compliance, including proper handling of client funds; failing to keep such records is a listed ground for discipline.
source_note: Ala. Code § 34-27-36(a); Ala. Admin. Code ch. 790-X-3 (record-keeping requirements). HEDGED: section/chapter-level citations, not independently live-verified this session.

topic: Violations Which May Result in Disciplinary Actions

choice_b: A violation, because failing to keep appropriate records of transactions is a listed ground for discipline
choice_c: A violation only if a client specifically complains about missing paperwork
choice_d: Acceptable as long as the broker's trust account bank statements are available
explanation: The inability to produce transaction records on request reflects a failure to keep appropriate records — an independent, listed ground for discipline, regardless of whether a client has separately complained.

topic: Violations Which May Result in Disciplinary Actions
question: A broker secretly pays a cash rebate to a buyer's mortgage loan officer, without the lender's knowledge, in exchange for the loan officer steering the buyer toward the broker's listings. Under Alabama license law, this undisclosed rebate arrangement is:
choice_a: Permitted, because rebates between real estate professionals are always lawful
choice_b: A violation only if the buyer ends up overpaying for the home
choice_c: A violation, because paying an undisclosed rebate or thing of value to influence a party's business decisions is grounds for discipline
choice_d: Permitted as long as the broker eventually discloses it to the buyer at closing
explanation: Secretly paying a rebate or other thing of value to influence a third party's professional judgment, without the knowledge of that person's employer or principal, is a recognized violation distinct from lawful, fully-disclosed rebate or fee arrangements.

topic: Violations Which May Result in Disciplinary Actions
question: Which of the following best distinguishes a lawful rebate from a prohibited one under Alabama license law?
choice_a: All rebates of any kind are strictly prohibited in every circumstance
choice_b: Rebates are lawful only when paid in cash rather than as a credit at closing
choice_c: Rebates are lawful only between two licensed brokers, never involving an unlicensed party
choice_d: A rebate disclosed to and consented to by the affected principal is generally lawful, while a secret, undisclosed rebate intended to influence a decision is a violation
explanation: The concern behind Alabama's rebate-related ground for discipline is concealment and undisclosed influence, not the mere existence of a rebate; a properly disclosed rebate to a principal generally does not raise the same violation.

topic: Violations Which May Result in Disciplinary Actions
question: A licensed broker pays a $2,000 finder's fee to an unlicensed neighbor for referring a buyer who purchased a home through the broker. Under Alabama license law, this payment is:
choice_a: A violation, because paying compensation to an unlicensed person for performing an act that requires a license is grounds for discipline
choice_b: Permitted, because anyone may be paid for simply mentioning a property to a friend
choice_c: Permitted as long as the fee is paid after closing rather than before
choice_d: A violation only if the unlicensed neighbor negotiated the purchase price
explanation: Paying a fee or commission to an unlicensed person for activity that constitutes licensed real estate brokerage — beyond a simple, non-negotiated name referral — is a listed violation, since it effectively compensates someone for unlicensed practice.

topic: Violations Which May Result in Disciplinary Actions
question: A salesperson accepts a commission check made out directly to the salesperson from a buyer, rather than having the funds flow through the salesperson's employing broker. Under Alabama license law, this is:
choice_a: Permitted, because any licensee may accept payment directly from a client

choice_c: A violation only if the broker later discovers the payment
choice_d: Permitted as long as the salesperson later reports the payment on a tax return
explanation: Alabama license law requires a salesperson's compensation for licensed activity to be paid through, and controlled by, the employing broker; accepting compensation directly and outside the broker's oversight is a listed violation.

topic: Violations Which May Result in Disciplinary Actions
question: A licensee pleads guilty to a felony theft charge unrelated to real estate. Under Alabama license law, the licensee's obligation regarding the Alabama Real Estate Commission is generally to:
choice_a: Do nothing, because the case did not involve a real estate transaction
choice_b: Inform only the licensee's employing broker, with no duty running to the Commission
choice_c: Inform the Commission of the plea and disposition of the case
choice_d: Inform the Commission only if the licensee is sentenced to jail time
explanation: Alabama license law requires a licensee to inform the Commission of certain adverse legal outcomes — including guilty pleas, convictions, or judgments — even when the underlying matter is not itself a real estate transaction; failing to do so is an independent ground for discipline.

topic: Violations Which May Result in Disciplinary Actions
question: A civil court enters a judgment against a licensee based on the licensee's fraud and misrepresentation in an unrelated business deal. Under Alabama license law, does the licensee have any duty toward the Real Estate Commission arising from that judgment?
choice_a: No — civil judgments never need to be reported to the Commission under any circumstances
choice_b: No — only judgments arising from a real estate transaction ever need to be reported
choice_c: Yes, but only if the licensee's broker instructs the licensee to report it
choice_d: Yes — the licensee must inform the Commission of a civil judgment based on fraud, misrepresentation, or deceit
explanation: Failure to inform the Commission of a civil judgment based on fraud, misrepresentation, or deceit is itself a listed ground for discipline, reflecting that such conduct bears on a licensee's fitness even outside a real estate transaction.

topic: Violations Which May Result in Disciplinary Actions
question: A brokerage runs a promotion stating that everyone who lists their home with the firm will be entered into a random drawing for a paid vacation, with the winner determined purely by chance. Under Alabama license law, this type of promotion is best described as:
choice_a: A prohibited lottery-type promotion tied to obtaining real estate business
choice_b: A standard, fully permitted marketing technique used by every brokerage
choice_c: Permitted as long as the vacation prize is worth less than the commission earned
choice_d: Permitted because the entrants are current clients rather than the general public
explanation: Conducting a lottery — a scheme combining prize, chance, and consideration (here, listing with the firm) — in connection with obtaining real estate business is expressly listed as a ground for discipline under Alabama license law.

topic: Violations Which May Result in Disciplinary Actions
question: A brokerage hosts a free open house and offers a drawing for a $25 gift card, open to any member of the public who walks in — no purchase, listing, or any form of consideration required to enter. Compared to a true lottery scheme, this promotion is:
choice_a: Identical to a prohibited lottery in every respect
choice_b: Generally distinguishable from a prohibited lottery, because it lacks the consideration element tying entry to real estate business
choice_c: A violation solely because a prize of any value was offered
choice_d: A violation only because it took place at an open house rather than an office
explanation: A lottery-type violation generally requires the combination of prize, chance, and consideration. A no-purchase, no-obligation drawing open to the general public lacks the consideration element tied to obtaining real estate business, distinguishing it from a prohibited scheme.
source_note: Ala. Code § 34-27-36(a) (lotteries — distinguished from a no-consideration public drawing). HEDGED: subsection (a) is confirmed real (see file note); the specific enumerated paragraph was not independently live-verified this session.

topic: Violations Which May Result in Disciplinary Actions
question: After a purchase agreement is signed by both the buyer and seller, the listing broker fails to give the buyer a copy of the fully executed contract despite the buyer's repeated requests. Under Alabama license law, this is:
choice_a: Not a violation, because only the seller is entitled to receive contract copies from the listing broker
choice_b: A violation only if the buyer suffers a financial loss as a result
choice_c: A violation, because failing to deliver a copy of a signed instrument to a party to the transaction is a listed ground for discipline
choice_d: Acceptable practice as long as the buyer's own agent has a copy
explanation: Alabama license law requires copies of signed instruments and contracts to be furnished to the parties who signed them; failing to deliver such documents on request is a listed handling-of-documents violation, regardless of whether the buyer's own agent separately has a copy.

topic: Violations Which May Result in Disciplinary Actions

choice_a: Permitted, because brokers may make minor administrative corrections to contracts at their discretion

question: The Alabama Real Estate Commission adopts a new rule under its administrative rulemaking authority governing how trust account deposits must be documented. A broker who knowingly disregards this rule has:

question: A licensee was previously disciplined by the Commission and placed on probation subject to specific conditions set out in the Commission's written order. The licensee later violates one of those probation conditions. Under Alabama law, this is:

topic: Violations Which May Result in Disciplinary Actions
question: A listing broker receives two written offers on the same property within an hour of each other but only presents the higher offer to the seller, never mentioning the second offer existed. Under Alabama license law, this is:
choice_a: Permitted, because a broker may use professional judgment to screen out weaker offers before presenting any to the seller

topic: Violations Which May Result in Disciplinary Actions
question: A seller has already signed a purchase agreement with one buyer, but the sale has not yet closed. A second buyer submits a written backup offer during this period. Under Alabama license law, the listing broker's obligation regarding the second offer is generally to:
choice_a: Present the backup offer to the seller, unless the seller has specifically and clearly instructed otherwise in writing
choice_b: Discard the backup offer automatically, since the property is already under contract
choice_c: Present the backup offer only to the buyer who is already under contract, not to the seller
choice_d: Hold the backup offer until the original closing falls through before mentioning it to anyone
